note: A WORKFLOW IS A DECLARATION. SmartPRS 2 answers its request screens from a 108 KB controller where every approval chain is written out in PHP, so a customer who wants one more approver above ₹50,000 needs a release. Here that is a threshold in this file. Each workflow names its subject, its steps, who decides each one, and the amount thresholds that route it. WHAT RUNS THEM, HONESTLY: Surface\\Requests, which is 384 lines of linear chain with amount routing. This note used to claim the generic Platform\\Workflow engine ran them and that no workflow-specific code existed anywhere, and that was simply false — the engine exists, is tested, and has parallel nodes, quorum, SLA timers, delegation and escalation, and nothing on any screen calls it. A configuration file that misdescribes its own engine is worse than one with no note: it is read by the person deciding whether a customer's requirement is a config change or a release, and it would have told them the wrong answer.

workflows.label: Leave request
workflows.subject: leaves
workflows.description: An employee asks for leave; their manager decides. Above ten days it also goes to HR, because a long absence is a staffing decision and not only a manager's.

steps.label: HR, because it is a long absence

workflows.label: Expense claim
workflows.subject: expenses
workflows.description: Reimbursement. Under ₹5,000 the manager finishes it; above that finance signs too, and above ₹50,000 so does the director.

workflows.label: Salary advance
workflows.subject: advances
workflows.description: An advance against salary. The HR Admin / HR Manager decides, alone (owner, 22 Sep): no Finance or Director step, whatever the amount. The step key stays 'finance' so requests already waiting on it are not stranded mid-chain; the label is what anybody sees.

workflows.label: Attendance regularisation
workflows.subject: attendance_corrections
workflows.description: A missing or wrong punch. The manager decides; nothing is written to attendance until they do.

workflows.label: Salary increment
workflows.subject: increments
workflows.description: A pay change. HR proposes, finance confirms the cost, the director signs — three people, because nobody should be able to change their own pay or anybody else's alone.

sla_note: `sla_hours` IS READ AND NOBODY IS TOLD. Surface\\Sla turns each open request's current step into the Node and Timer values Platform\\Workflow\\Sla\\Sweep decides about, so a step past its due-within is reported as breached, dated from the deadline rather than from when the sweep ran, and coalesced into one digest per approver. What does NOT happen: no notification, no reminder, no escalation, no reassignment, no automatic decision. There is no notification channel in this build, so at hour 49 of a 48-hour SLA the request appears on an overdue report and the approver hears nothing. `php tools/workflow-sweep.php --tenant=<id>` runs it and exits non-zero on a breach. A step that declares no sla_hours is reported as its own state and never counted as within SLA — nobody set it a deadline, which is not the same as keeping one.
